- If sentiment history shows increasing bullish sentiment (e.g., >0.20 in recent days), model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction.
- If model shows gradual upward trend with no spike, but true outcome has sharp spike later, model underestimates near-term volatility; adjust forecast to include early breakout.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overcorrects and underestimates subsequent rally; add 2–5% buffer to forecast for momentum continuation.
- If sentiment is neutral or bearish (0.00 or low), model often fails to capture downward drift; apply slight downward adjustment to avoid overconfidence.
- Model tends to lag in early periods (first 3–5 days of forecast) — especially when sentiment is low — and underestimates volatility; add 1–3% upward adjustment for early horizon.
- When true outcome shows mean reversion after a spike, model often fails to recognize it; reduce forecast slope after peak and add smoothing factor (e.g., 0.8x prior trend).
- If sentiment history includes multiple 0.00 entries followed by a spike, model often misses the spike; use sentiment as trigger to increase forecast slope by 10–20% for next 3–5 days.
